note: Language-neutral expectations. A renderer in ANY language is correct when it satisfies these, and not before. Inputs are the ones the core actually produces: terms already split on whitespace with quotes stripped.

matchParam.why: several terms: a conjunction in every dialect
the core strips quotes, so user input cannot break the expression
terms the engine tokenises as one token must stay one term

sqlite: CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE IF NOT EXISTS messages_fts USING fts5(subject, fromaddr, body_text, content='messages', content_rowid='rowid', tokenize='unicode61')
turso: CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS messages_fts ON messages USING fts (subject, fromaddr, body_text)
postgres: ALTER TABLE messages ADD COLUMN messages_fts tsvector GENERATED ALWAYS AS (to_tsvector('simple', coalesce(subject,'') || ' ' || coalesce(fromaddr,'') || ' ' || coalesce(body_text,''))) STORED
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS messages_fts_idx ON messages USING GIN (messages_fts)

ftsSync.why: the core emits NO runtime sync statements on any engine: sqlite is 'triggers' (the schema owns upkeep), turso and postgres are 'engine' (the engine owns it). A hand-maintained DELETE is not merely unnecessary — it is invalid, see the engine's fts.traps.

ftsTriggers.why: the schema-owned trio. Required for sqlite: removal needs the documented 'delete' command carrying the OLD column values, which only a trigger has.
sqlite: CREATE TRIGGER IF NOT EXISTS messages_fts_ai AFTER INSERT ON messages BEGIN INSERT INTO messages_fts(rowid, subject, fromaddr, body_text) VALUES (new.rowid, new.subject, new.fromaddr, new.body_text); END

CREATE TRIGGER IF NOT EXISTS messages_fts_ad AFTER DELETE ON messages BEGIN INSERT INTO messages_fts(messages_fts, rowid, subject, fromaddr, body_text) VALUES ('delete', old.rowid, old.subject, old.fromaddr, old.body_text); END

CREATE TRIGGER IF NOT EXISTS messages_fts_au AFTER UPDATE ON messages WHEN old.subject IS NOT new.subject OR old.fromaddr IS NOT new.fromaddr OR old.body_text IS NOT new.body_text BEGIN INSERT INTO messages_fts(messages_fts, rowid, subject, fromaddr, body_text) VALUES ('delete', old.rowid, old.subject, old.fromaddr, old.body_text); INSERT INTO messages_fts(rowid, subject, fromaddr, body_text) VALUES (new.rowid, new.subject, new.fromaddr, new.body_text); END

search.why: select and orderBy are identical across engines because every dialect aliases the table as m

sqlite.sql: SELECT m.uid, m.folder, m.subject, m.fromaddr, m.internaldate FROM messages_fts f JOIN messages m ON m.rowid = f.rowid WHERE messages_fts MATCH ? ORDER BY m.internaldate DESC LIMIT ?

turso.sql: SELECT m.uid, m.folder, m.subject, m.fromaddr, m.internaldate FROM messages m WHERE fts_match(subject, fromaddr, body_text, ?) ORDER BY m.internaldate DESC LIMIT ?

postgres.sql: SELECT m.uid, m.folder, m.subject, m.fromaddr, m.internaldate FROM messages m WHERE messages_fts @@ plainto_tsquery('simple', ?) ORDER BY m.internaldate DESC LIMIT ?

failClosed.why: an engine the tables do not describe must throw, never fall back to a default dialect
